Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

orderStatMoments 0.3.0

  • Eight families are added, so that the built-in families are the twelve continuous distributions for which base R provides the p, d and q functions, and the Gumbel: "t", "cauchy", "gamma", "chisq", "beta", "lnorm", "weibull" and "f" join "norm", "unif", "exp", "logis" and "gumbel". The package sets their supports and their tail indices, so a moment that does not exist (the variance of the minimum of a Cauchy sample) is refused without a declaration by the user. The noncentral versions (R’s ncp) are not built in.
  • A built-in family is given as in R. Its parameters are passed to os_moments() by R’s own names, with R’s defaults: os_moments(10, dist = "gamma", shape = 2, rate = 3), os_moments(10, dist = "norm", mean = 3, sd = 2). The package splits them into the shape parameters, which define the standard member it integrates, and a shift and a multiplier, which it applies exactly afterwards.
  • The arguments location and scale of os_moments() are replaced by os_shift and os_multiplier, the constants a and b > 0 of a + bX, which apply to any distribution. Code that passed location or scale needs the family’s own parameter (mean and sd for the normal, rate for the exponential, min and max for the uniform) or the two new arguments. The logistic keeps location and scale, which are its parameters in R, and so does the Gumbel, which R does not provide and whose parameters the package names in the same way. A call with a parameter that the family does not have stops with a message that names the right one. Every argument after dist is given by its full name.
  • The object that os_moments() returns stores par, os_shift, os_multiplier and affine in place of location and scale.
  • A density that is infinite at a finite endpoint of the support (a gamma, a chi-square, a Weibull, a beta or an F distribution with a shape below 1) is integrated next to that endpoint in a variable in which the integrand is bounded. Such distributions are computed where the previous version stopped with an error (a Weibull with shape 0.5 at the minimum of 101, a gamma with shape 0.1 at any sample size). An extreme order statistic that concentrates against the endpoint is computed in the distance from it: the tests assert the minimum of a million observations from a beta(a, 1), at a = 0.5, 0.1 and 0.05, against its exact moments, within 1e-10 for the mean and 1e-9 for the variance in relative terms. The moments of a distribution whose density is finite at its endpoints, and for which no breaks are declared, are computed by the same calls as before and are unchanged.
  • os_dist() takes a new argument breaks, the points inside the support at which the density of a user-supplied distribution has a kink or a jump (the median of the Laplace distribution, the mode of a triangular distribution). os_moments() cuts every integral at these points, because the quadrature rule assumes a smooth integrand inside each piece. For the Laplace distribution at n = 5, the covariances sum to their exact value within 1e-12 with breaks = 0, and within about 1e-8 without it. The density may be zero at a declared point. The built-in families have no such point.
  • The F family computes its quantiles through qbeta() in each tail, because R’s qf() loses the digits of a small quantile (it returns 0 at p = 1e-4 for df1 = 0.5 and df2 = 10).
  • The help page of os_moments() lists the cases on which the accuracy has been tested. They include cases chosen because they are hard: a density that is infinite at an endpoint with an index down to 0.025, sample sizes up to 1e7, and variances that barely exist.
  • The help pages, the vignette and the README are rewritten for the new interface. They present the numerical design in three parts (what is computed, how it is integrated, how the integrand is evaluated), and the example of a user-supplied distribution is a Pareto distribution.
  • os_blue() returns the weights and the variance factors of the two estimators under names that say which parameter of the location-scale family they belong to: w_mu and w_sigma (formerly w_location and w_scale), and var_mu and var_sigma (formerly var_location and var_scale). cov, ranks, n and dist are unchanged. The former names read like the arguments location and scale of os_moments(), which are known constants that shift and scale the distribution, whereas os_blue() estimates the unknown location and scale parameters of the family. Code that reads the old names needs the new ones. The computation is unchanged.

orderStatMoments 0.2.0

  • The package is renamed orderStatMoments, from osmoments, so that its name says what it computes. The functions keep their names (os_moments(), os_dist(), os_quantile_weights(), os_lin_moments(), os_blue()). The object that os_moments() returns now has class "orderStatMoments" (formerly "osmoments"), and its print method is renamed with it. Install with remotes::install_github("ZWuLab/orderStatMoments"). The former repository address redirects there.
  • The vignette’s Appendix A and the help page of os_moments() say “approach” where they said “device” for the four numerical approaches of the computation. The code is unchanged.
